A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AlgoVeri benchmark and provide readable text, tables, figures, and complete Appendices A–D. The appendix pages are identical in text and rendering, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of six models in Table 2, alongside algorithm-category results, repair-versus-sampling experiments, and failure analyses in Figures 3–6.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds GPT-5.3 Codex evaluations across Dafny, Verus, and Lean in Table 2.

M1.justification: The aligned specifications, expert curation, compiler-feedback repair pipeline, and semantic filtering remain unchanged. GPT-5.3 Codex is an additional evaluated model, not a new method component; Appendix C's prompts are identical.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 77 classical algorithm problems across Dafny, Verus, and Lean. The task categories and Appendix D's specification examples are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds GPT-5.3 Codex to the evaluated comparison set while retaining Gemini-3 Flash, GPT-5 mini, GPT-OSS-120B, both Qwen3 models, and Devstral-2-123B.

E3.justification: The new Codex evaluation uses a 1×8 budget, explicitly described as eight repair rounds. Existing 1×15 and 10×15 evaluations and metrics remain unchanged. However, Section 3's general statement and Table 2's caption still describe a uniform 15-round protocol.

E4.justification: The category breakdown, repair-depth trajectories, equal-generation-budget sampling comparison, and failure analyses in Figures 3–6 are unchanged. No corresponding Codex ablation or diagnostic analysis is added.

E5.justification: Existing ± reporting for open-weight models is unchanged. Codex receives point estimates, following the existing proprietary-model reporting practice, without new seed information, uncertainty estimates, or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds Codex compiler-verified/semantically filtered percentages of 49.35/42.86 for Dafny, 14.29/11.69 for Verus, and 23.38/11.69 for Lean. All previously reported values and plotted results are retained. These are additional results at a different repair budget, not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: Section 2.3's specification checks and the formal definitions, example proofs, and specifications in Appendices A and D are unchanged. No mathematical assumption, derivation, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution summary, and conclusion retain the same claims about aligned algorithmic verification, differences between verification systems, and repair dynamics. Codex adds supporting evidence without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning algorithmic fidelity, global reasoning, syntax/search barriers, and depth versus width remain unchanged. Qualifications about non-idiomatic Lean specifications and the limits of specification-based correctness are also retained.

D1.justification: Section 3 and Table 2 supply the new Codex experiment's 1×8 configuration, a limited addition to reproducibility information. The model-details appendix, prompt templates, and code/data access information are unchanged; Table 3 does not add a Codex version identifier.

R1.justification: v2 adds foundational citations for Dafny (Leino, 2010), Verus (Lattuada et al., 2023), and Lean (Moura and Ullrich, 2021). The benchmark's relationship to prior work remains unchanged. The revised StepProver bibliography entry identifies the same work, rather than adding another cited study.

P1.justification: Edits are localized: Section 3 gains the Codex mention and result sentence, punctuation and bibliographic metadata are adjusted, and the preprint notice becomes an ICML proceedings notice. The section organization and substantive narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains a Codex row and is enlarged. Figures 1 and 5 are also enlarged without changing their content, producing some text reflow. The remaining plots and appendix layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The additional Codex evaluation provides a useful reference point for benchmark difficulty across all three verification systems, while the foundational citations improve attribution. These are limited benefits: the eight-round experiment is inconsistently covered by the retained 15-round description and lacks a model-details entry in Table 3, reducing comparison clarity and reproducibility.
